findings.title: Every functional and technical success criterion maps to a task
findings.description:
Each success criterion has a task that implements it:
- Fresh-clone `cf build` and `--json` output: Tasks 19–21.
- `cf guides info` shows "Checkout: not initialized" without changing anything: Tasks 10, 11 and 24.
- Out-of-sync warning that changes nothing: Tasks 17, 18 and 21.
- `--strategy manual` alias: Tasks 1, 7 and 8.
- `manual` in config is treated as tarball: Tasks 5 and 6.
- `cf init --strategy` and the help text: Tasks 25–27.
- Managed-directory line and README: Tasks 28–30.
- Malformed config fails instead of falling back: Tasks 5 and 6.
- The grep checks and CHANGELOG/DEVLOG: Tasks 31 and 32.

Nothing is scope creep. The `gitExec` timeout (Tasks 13–14) traces to D10, and `guide_status` checkout reporting traces to Component Structure. No NFR is restated, so no load test or CI task is needed. Test tasks follow their implementation tasks throughout.

findings.title: The commits after Task 4 and Task 6 leave the MCP package failing typecheck
findings.description:
`guide_install` declares `z.enum(['submodule', 'clone', 'manual'])` and passes `strategy` straight to `manager.install(strategy, source)` at line 116. Once Task 1 narrows `GuideMethod` to `'submodule' | 'clone' | 'tarball'`, `'manual'` can no longer be assigned to the parameter, so `@context-forge/mcp-server` stops typechecking. Task 7 is the first task that fixes it.

The commits at Task 4 (`refactor(core): rename…`) and Task 6 (`fix(core): …drop silent catches`) only check core (`pnpm --filter @context-forge/core test`). Both therefore commit a workspace that does not build.

Fix: move the MCP enum/normalize change and the CLI `as GuideMethod` cast removal into Task 3 (or just before the Task 4 commit). Change the Task 4 success criterion to `pnpm -r typecheck` so the commit happens at a working point.

findings.title: Commit markers are inside checkbox items, so commits will default to once per task, including after the non-compiling Task 1
findings.description:
Every commit is written as "Commit: `…`" inside a `- [ ] Success criteria:` checkbox. There are no plain `**Commit**:` lines. Under the project rule, a file with no markers commits "at the end of each top-level task." That means a commit after Task 1, whose own success criterion says core typecheck *fails* until Task 3, and after Tasks 3, 5, 9, 10, 13, 15 and so on.

Fix: pull each commit out into a plain `**Commit**: \`…\`` line after the relevant task (4, 6, 8, 12, 14, 16, 18, 21, 23, 24, 27, 29, 31, 32). Alternatively, merge Task 1 into Task 3 so no task ends with code that doesn't compile.

findings.title: Task 15 is ambiguous about where the timeout is applied, and no test checks that auto-init is time-bounded
findings.description:
Task 15 contradicts itself:
- It says `init()` "runs … with `{ timeoutMs: GUIDE_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS }`".
- It also says to "pass the timeout as an `init()` option so `sync()` and `update()` keep unbounded behavior."

Task 17 then calls `SubmoduleStrategy.init(operationPath)` with no option. A junior implementer could reasonably make the timeout opt-in, which leaves the auto-init path unbounded. That breaks D10 and leaves F004 (the hang case) unresolved. Tasks 16 and 18 don't check which timeout reaches `gitExec`, and Task 14 only tests `gitExec` on its own.

Fix: state one signature, e.g. `init(path, opts: { timeoutMs?: number })`, with `ensureCheckout()` passing `GUIDE_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS` and `sync()` passing nothing. Add one assertion to Task 18 that the `ensureCheckout()` → `init()` path calls `gitExec` with `timeoutMs === GUIDE_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS`, and one to Task 16 that `sync()` passes no timeout.

findings.title: Task 11 makes `detect()` throw, which differs from the design and changes behavior for every caller
findings.description:
The design's Data Flow puts `'error' → throw` inside `ensureCheckout()`. D3 also requires `cf guides info` to stay a read-only status command a user "can always inspect first." Task 11 puts the throw inside `GuideDetector.detect()` instead.

`detect()` is also called by `cf guides info`, `guide_status`, `setup-ide`, install and update. With this change, a submodule install in an environment where git is missing or the directory isn't a repo would stop the status commands from working at all, rather than reporting the problem. Task 12 also has no test for the `'error'` branch.

Fix: either set `checkout` to the error state (or `null`) in `detect()` and throw only in `ensureCheckout()` as the design specifies, or record that this decision was made deliberately. In either case, add a test for the `'error'` branch.

findings.title: The Task 9 fixture will fail on current git unless file-protocol submodules are allowed, and the test pattern it points to doesn't exist
findings.description:
Task 9 builds a host repo that adds a local bare repo as a submodule. It then runs `git submodule update --init`, both in the fixture and through `SubmoduleStrategy.init()` → `gitExec`. Since git 2.38.1, `protocol.file.allow` defaults to `user`, so local-path submodule clones fail with "transport 'file' not allowed." The fixture and every test using the `cloned()` state (Tasks 12, 16, 18, 21, 23, 24) would fail.

Separately, the Context Summary says `SubmoduleStrategy.test.ts` is "the place to look for an existing real-git temp-repo pattern." That file is mocked ("calls submodule add, git add, and git commit"), so there is no such pattern to extend.

Fix: tell Task 9 to configure `protocol.file.allow=always` in a way that also reaches the child processes `gitExec` starts, e.g. `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0`/`GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0` in the test environment or a temp `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`. Correct the Context Summary to say no real-git helper exists yet.

findings.title: No CLI test for the deprecation warning when `manual` comes from config
findings.description:
The success criterion says a project with `guide.git_strategy: manual` "installs as tarball with the same warning." Task 6 checks that core reports the alias, and Task 7 prints the warning in `guidesInstallAction()`. But Task 8 only tests the `--strategy manual` flag path, so nothing checks that the config path actually prints the warning to stderr.

Fix: add one case to Task 8: config contains `manual`, then `cf guides install` writes the deprecation line to stderr and `guides info --json` reports `tarball`.

findings.title: Task 26 calls `normalizeGuideMethod(opts.strategy)` without saying what happens when the flag is omitted
findings.description:
If `--strategy` isn't given, `opts.strategy` is `undefined`. Normalizing it unconditionally would throw, or fail typecheck, and break plain `cf init`. Say that normalization runs only when the flag is present and that otherwise the config/default path in `guidesInstallAction` is used. Also add a `cf init` case without `--strategy` to Task 27.

The alias-warning text is now produced at three CLI sites: the install flag, install via config, and init. A small shared helper next to `GUIDE_STRATEGIES` would keep that text in one place.

findings.title: Some grep and mock-based checks are weaker than they look
findings.description:
- Task 7's `grep -rn "manual"` (unquoted) also matches words like "manually" in comments, so it can fail when nothing is wrong. Use `"'manual'"` or a word-boundary pattern.
- Task 27 checks that "no `.gitmodules` is created" while also checking that `guidesInstallAction` was called. If that action is mocked, the `.gitmodules` check proves nothing. Make it either a real tarball install or a check of the arguments only.
- Task 6(c) mocks `ConfigManager.get()` to throw. One test using a real malformed config file would confirm that `get()` actually throws in that case, which is what the "malformed shared config" criterion depends on.

findings.title: A few tasks are small enough to merge
findings.description:
32 tasks is reasonable for three issues spread across core, CLI and MCP. A few merges would cut overhead and remove broken intermediate states:
- Task 1 into Task 3 (removes the non-compiling Task 1 state).
- Task 10 into Task 11 (Task 10's own success criterion depends on Task 11).
- Task 28 into Task 29.
